beats.text: A knife is made for cutting. Its purpose exists before the knife does.
Sartre said humans are the opposite. We exist first — and only then invent what we are for.
No fixed nature, no blueprint, no script. Existence precedes essence.
That sounds like freedom, and it is. It is also a weight. Every choice is yours to own.
So we hide. We say 'I had no choice,' 'that's just how I am.' Sartre called this bad faith.
Pretending you aren't free is the one lie that costs you your life while you're still living it.
You are not a knife. You are the one deciding, right now, what you are for.

attribution: Jean-Paul Sartre · Existentialism Is a Humanism
